verdict.topBlocker: The Gmail scopes an agent needs (readonly, modify, compose) are restricted: brand verification, then ~6-week restricted-scope verification ending in a CASA assessment paid to a third-party assessor and renewed yearly.
verdict.summary: Before customers outside your Workspace can connect, you need brand verification (2-3 business days) and restricted-scope verification including CASA (Google estimates ~6 weeks; a gmail.send-only app needs ~10 business days and no CASA). A Workspace Marketplace listing is optional, and the limits that bite are the 100-user lifetime cap while unverified, 7-day tokens in Testing, customer admins who must trust the app for restricted Gmail access, and per-user Gmail quotas.
verdict.reason: approvalWait min raised from 14 to 42 days because 14 only fits a sensitive-only (gmail.send) app while the verdict is about restricted scopes; difficulty 5 and effort range kept (effort is not officially stated).

optionalPaths.name: Google Workspace Marketplace public listing
optionalPaths.why: For vendors who want Workspace admins to discover and domain-install the app; not needed for OAuth and requires OAuth verification first; Google only says 'several days'.

optionalPaths.name: Marketplace CASA independent security badge (AL2)
optionalPaths.why: For vendors selling to security-conscious Workspace buyers; reuses an AL2 CASA result and the badge can take up to three weeks to appear.
optionalPaths.evidence: https://developers.google.com/workspace/marketplace/get-featured - "it can take up to three weeks for the badge to appear on your store listing"

optionalPaths.name: Recommended for Google Workspace program
optionalPaths.why: Marketing visibility for mature apps; Google evaluates applicants once a year and requires CASA AL2.
optionalPaths.evidence: https://developers.google.com/workspace/marketplace/get-featured - Recommended for Google Workspace: Google evaluates apps once a year

limits.limit: 100 new users lifetime cap for apps showing the unverified app screen
limits.impact: Without completed restricted-scope verification, a multi-customer agent stops onboarding after 100 users and the cap never resets.
limits.evidence: https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945 - "100 new users in total, after the app presents the unverified app screen"

limits.limit: Testing status: 100 test users; authorizations and refresh tokens expire after 7 days
limits.impact: Testing mode cannot serve real customers; agents would need re-consent weekly.
limits.evidence: https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945 - "Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent."

limits.limit: Refresh tokens: 100 per account per client; revoked after 6 months unused or on password change for Gmail scopes
limits.impact: Agents must handle invalid_grant and re-prompt; idle background agents lose access.
limits.evidence: https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2 - "The user changed passwords and the refresh token contains Gmail scopes."

limits.limit: Gmail API quota: 1,200,000 units/min per project, 6,000 units/min per user (messages.send = 100 units)
limits.impact: One user's agent can send at most ~60 messages a minute via the API and bulk reads must be throttled.
limits.evidence: https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/quota - per minute per user per project "6,000 quota units"

limits.limit: Customer Workspace admin controls: Trusted / Limited / Blocked; Limited apps cannot use restricted services
limits.impact: Even after verification, business customers whose admins restrict Gmail must mark the agent Trusted before restricted Gmail scopes work.
limits.evidence: https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/control-which-apps-access-google-workspace-data - Limited: "App can only access unrestricted services."

limits.limit: Annual re-verification and CASA revalidation every 12 months
limits.impact: Recurring yearly cost and work; lapsing risks restricted-scope access for every customer.
limits.evidence: https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/production-readiness/restricted-scope-verification - "complete a security assessment at least every 12 months"

limits.limit: Limited Use: no AI/ML model training on Gmail data beyond that user's personalized model
limits.impact: An AI agent cannot use customer mail to train or improve general models.
limits.evidence: https://developers.google.com/workspace/workspace-api-user-data-developer-policy - no using user data "to create, train, or improve a machine learning or artificial intelligence model"

stepChanges.newTitle: Create a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
stepChanges.newDetail: In the Google Cloud console create a project, enable the Gmail API and open Google Auth Platform. Billing is not listed as a prerequisite.
stepChanges.reason: Billing is not a Gmail API prerequisite; the Gmail quickstart lists only a Cloud project.

stepChanges.newTitle: Publish a privacy policy (terms of service optional)
stepChanges.newDetail: Host a privacy policy on the same domain as your public home page, covering Gmail data use and Limited Use, and link it from both the home page and the consent screen. Terms of service are optional.
stepChanges.reason: Brand verification page treats ToS as optional; the privacy policy must share the home page domain.

stepChanges.newTitle: Add authorized domains and create a Web OAuth client
stepChanges.newDetail: Add the top private domains used by your redirect URIs and app links to Authorized domains, register exact HTTPS redirect URIs (localhost exempt), and store the client secret securely. Verify domain ownership in Search Console before brand verification.
stepChanges.reason: Search Console verification is a brand-verification requirement, not a prerequisite for redirect URIs; the auth-endpoint link does not belong on this step.

stepChanges.newTitle: Configure audience (External), branding, data access scopes and test users
stepChanges.newDetail: Set Audience to External (Internal only works inside your own Workspace org), fill branding, add the narrowest Gmail scopes, and add up to 100 test users.
stepChanges.reason: Guide omits the External user type choice, which decides whether outside customers can connect at all.

stepChanges.newTitle: Run the authorization code flow with offline access
stepChanges.newDetail: Use https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth with access_type=offline (and prompt=consent when a new refresh token is needed), PKCE S256 optional, and exchange codes at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token.
stepChanges.reason: Without access_type=offline no refresh token is issued, which a background agent needs.

stepChanges.newTitle: Verify branding, then submit data-access verification
stepChanges.newDetail: On the Branding page click Verify Branding and publish within 7 days; then in the Verification Center declare all sensitive/restricted scopes with justification, demo video and documentation links.
stepChanges.reason: Brand verification must be published before scope verification; they are separate submissions.

stepChanges.newTitle: Complete the CASA security assessment (restricted scopes)
stepChanges.newDetail: When Google's Trust and Safety team notifies you, scan the app, fix failed CWEs, submit results to a Google-authorized assessor and obtain a Letter of Validation; renew yearly. Google charges nothing; you pay the assessor (Google's Health API page cites $500-$4,500 and 2-3 weeks for tier 2).
stepChanges.reason: Owner should be you plus the assessor, not provider with 0 minutes; Google does publish a cost range elsewhere.
